promptLatex: Two fair coins are flipped. What is the probability that the two coins show the same face?
hintLatex: There are four equally likely pairs of results.
Three of the pairs have two identical faces: heads-heads, tails-tails, and heads-tails in either order gives two more.
Of those $4$ outcomes, $2$ have the same face on both coins.
solutionLatex:
Two flips of a fair coin give $4$ equally likely outcomes: $(H,H)$, $(H,T)$, $(T,H)$ and $(T,T)$.

Two of these have the same face on both coins, namely $(H,H)$ and $(T,T)$.

Therefore $P = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$. This also follows by independence: $P(H \cap H) + P(T \cap T) = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.
